Problem: The entire review judge command hangs indefinitely when the provider CLI backgrounds a sandbox or MCP grandchild that inherits the output pipe. +// must kill the whole group — otherwise the read blocks for the full sleep.
+func TestTerminateOnCancel_KillsProcessGroup(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	defer cancel()
+
+	// `sleep 60 &` backgrounds a grandchild that holds stdout; "ready" prints after
+	// it backgrounds so we cancel strictly after it exists (no race). `wait` keeps
+	// the shell alive as group leader so only a group-wide kill ends both.
+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 60 & echo ready; wait")
+	TerminateOnCancel(cmd)
+
+	stdout, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("stdout pipe: %v", err)
+	}
+	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	// Wait for "ready" so the grandchild is up and holding the pipe.
+	br := bufio.NewReader(stdout)
+	if line, err := br.ReadString('\n'); err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(line) != "ready" {
+		t.Fatalf("did not observe ready marker: line=%q err=%v", line, err)
+	}
+
+	done := make(chan error, 1)
+	go func() {
+		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, br) //nolint:errcheck // draining to block until the pipe closes; copy errors are irrelevant
+		done <- cmd.Wait()
+	}()

+

+	// the pipe closed on its own, letting this test pass even if group-kill regressed.
+	select {

+	}

+	}

+	// regression would block on the full 60s sleep instead of failing fast.

+		}

Reviewed trail #1153 (`fix/review-judge-hang-terminate-on-cancel`, 1 commit, ad19dcc1f). Build, `mise run lint` (0 issues), and the package tests all pass on a clean checkout of the branch.

The extraction into `execx.TerminateOnCancel` is right, and the diagnosis is correct — with `cmd.Stdout` as a `bytes.Buffer`, exec spawns a copy goroutine on a real pipe, so a grandchild holding the write end blocks `Wait` past the deadline. The problem is where it's applied.

## The judge's default provider is still unfixed

`defaultJudge` (`review/profile.go:405`) prefers **claude-code** first among configured reviewers. `AgentSynthesisProvider.Synthesize` (`review/synthesis_sink.go:56`) calls `tg.GenerateText`, and `ClaudeCodeAgent` deliberately does *not* route through `RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI` — it runs its own exec at `claudecode/generate.go:174-186`, with no `TerminateOnCancel`. I ran the branch's own reproduction against it:

```go
CommandRunner: exec.CommandContext(ctx, "/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 60 & echo ready; wait")
ctx deadline: 300ms
→ HUNG: GenerateText did not return 20s after a 300ms deadline
```

So `entire review`'s judge still hangs forever in the default configuration. The judge's default bound is 20m (`defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout`), and it isn't reached — the deadline can't unblock a held pipe, which is the whole point of the fix. The five providers that *do* go through the shared helper (codex, cursor, gemini, copilot, pi) are fixed.

## Same gap on the streaming path

`claudecode/generate_streaming.go` has the same shape and also hangs (verified, same probe). It's worse there: it blocks in `io.Copy(io.Discard, counted)` at line 78 *before* `cmd.Wait()`, so without `WaitDelay` nothing force-closes the pipe. The comment above that drain — "Without this, a blocked pipe would deadlock cmd.Wait()" — is only true for the direct child. That path is reached from `entire explain --generate` and from post-commit condensation (`manual_commit_condensation.go:1015`), where `summarizeCtx` carries no deadline at all.

Both are three-line changes mirroring the one you made in `text_generator_cli.go`.

## Smaller things

**Exported contract change, undocumented** (`text_generator_cli.go:48`). Setting `Cancel` on a cmd the helper didn't create means an injected `TextCommandRunner` must now use `exec.CommandContext`. Verified failure:

```
failed to run echo CLI: exec: command with a non-nil Cancel was not created with CommandContext
```

Production is safe (every caller passes nil or a nil field) and every current test runner uses `CommandContext`, but the `TextCommandRunner` doc at line 30 still just says "matches exec.CommandContext" — worth stating the requirement there, since the error names a field the runner author never set.

**`NonInteractive` + `TerminateOnCancel` fails with a misleading error, guarded only by a doc comment.** Confirmed: `fork/exec /bin/echo: operation not permitted` — which reads as a sandbox problem, not misuse. A guard makes them compose, because `setsid` already makes the child its own process-group leader so `kill(-pid)` still works:

```go
if !cmd.SysProcAttr.Setsid {
    cmd.SysProcAttr.Setpgid = true
}
```

I applied that in a scratch worktree and the group-kill test still passes promptly (`err=signal: killed`, well under `KillWaitDelay/2`).

**Duplicate test.** `TestTerminateOnCancel_KillsProcessGroup` is now byte-identical in `checkpoint/remote/command_cancel_unix_test.go` and `execx/execx_unix_test.go`, and the remote copy exercises a one-line pass-through. Lint doesn't flag it, so this is taste — but dropping the remote copy and keeping `TestKillProcessGroupOnCancel_SetsSetpgidAndCancel` (which does verify `newCommand`'s wiring) would leave the coverage intact.

**The new agent-level test doesn't pin group-kill.** `TestRunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI_ReturnsOnDeadlineWithPipeHoldingGrandchild` uses a `KillWaitDelay + 5s` deadline, so it passes on the 10s backstop alone if group-kill regresses. Its comment is honest about this, and the execx twin correctly uses `KillWaitDelay/2` — just noting nothing at the agent layer catches a group-kill regression.

**Ctrl-C.** `Setpgid` takes the provider CLI out of the terminal's foreground group, so it no longer receives terminal SIGINT and depends on `main.go`'s cancel → group SIGKILL. That works, but the second-Ctrl-C path (`dieFromSignal`) exits `entire` immediately and can orphan the provider. Same tradeoff already accepted for git in `checkpoint/remote`, so probably fine — worth knowing it now applies to provider CLIs too.

I haven't posted anything to the trail. Want me to file the claude-code gap as a finding, or write the fix for the two Claude Code paths?

---
name: no-fluff-in-review-artifacts
description: "Keep trail findings, PR comments and review write-ups short; no self-justifying prose"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 96153156-a452-4cf3-890f-3b0ece545107
  modified: 2026-08-13T15:47:02.376Z
---

Stefan, on trail findings I posted 2-4x longer than my chat summary of the same
points (2026-08-13, trail #1039): "why are the findings so much longer than what
you wrote me here?" then "don't add so much fluff, nobody reads that either".
Trimmed 113-271 words down to 26-106 and that was the right length.

**Why:** a finding is read cold by the owner who then decides. It does not need
to sell itself, and length actively costs readership — the padding makes the
mechanism harder to find, not better supported.

**How to apply:** in findings, PR comments and review write-ups, keep the
mechanism, the `file:line` of any second occurrence, the suggested diff, and one
line of verification evidence. Cut:

- topic sentences that argue for the finding's own importance ("The failure mode
  is what makes this worth a line of insurance rather than a shrug")
- meta-commentary on my own severity or stance ("Flagging for the future, not
  asking for a change here — I think leaving this alone is the right call")
- "Worth fixing because…" framing on nits — a stale comment gets one sentence
- explaining the same mechanism both before and after a code block

The tell is a finding that opens by justifying itself. Severity and location
already do that job. Do not expand a chat-length point when writing it to a
durable artifact; the cold reader needs *context* (the second file, the repro),
not *persuasion*.

Related: [[deslop-unwired-functions]].

---
name: trail-write-gotchas
description: "entire trail write gotchas: the body has its own PUT route (the old PATCH 503 was a wrong-route bug), labels are not writable, and probing safely needs a scratch trail with a branch"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Gotchas when exercising `entire trail` **writes** against entire-api.

There is no backend switch to set: `ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND` was removed on
2026-08-18 and entire-api is the only backend, so writes work by default. (The
old advice to export that var is dead — don't go looking for it.)

- **A trail's description is written by `PUT .../trails/{host}/{owner}/{repo}/{number}/body`, never by the trail PATCH.**
  The PATCH route answers a `body` field with an unconditional 503, and the API
  redacts 5xx messages, so the caller sees a bare "Service Unavailable" — which
  is why the earlier probe (2026-08-17, trail #1017, 200 B–4 KB, retried over
  ~10 minutes) read as a flaky server or a size limit. It was neither: wrong
  route. Fixed in the CLI on 2026-08-19 (`sendTrailBody` in `trail_cmd.go`);
  `api.TrailUpdateRequest` deliberately has no `Body` field so the mistake
  cannot be re-made. The PUT takes `{markdown, overwrite}` (or `contentJson`
  instead of `markdown`) and **refuses a non-empty description with 409
  `document_not_empty` unless `overwrite: true`** — that flag is what makes
  editing an existing description work at all. Its `If-Match` alternative is
  unusable from a read: the ETag comes only from this route's own response
  header, and `bodyDocument.updatedAt` from a trail read is formatted to a
  different precision, so a reconstructed header never matches.
- **Labels are read-only.** `--add-label`/`--remove-label` no longer exist; the
  API accepts no label writes. Reads (`trail show`'s `Labels:` line) still work.
- **Probing safely needs a scratch trail *with* a branch.** `trail update` can
  only target a trail **by branch**, so a `--no-branch` scratch trail is
  unpatchable — but creating one with `--branch` also **creates and pushes that
  branch to origin**. Clean up both the trail and the remote branch afterwards.

Related: [[trail-tune-command]], [[no-fluff-in-review-artifacts]]

PR #2150 is up: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2150

It covers all six findings from the trail. The substantive part:

**The judge was still hanging after #2140.** That PR bounded `RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI`, which covers codex/cursor/gemini/copilot/pi — but Claude Code runs the CLI itself on both its text-generation paths, and `defaultJudge` prefers claude-code. The rest: the `Setsid`/`Setpgid` conflict is now handled instead of just warned about (they compose, group-kill still works), the `TextCommandRunner` contract is documented, the loose deadline test is tightened to `KillWaitDelay/2`, and the duplicated test is gone.

Each new test was verified red on the pre-fix tree and green after — including reverting the two source hunks to confirm the claudecode tests actually fail without them.

Two things worth knowing:

- I had to add `execx` to the allowlist in `architecture_test.go`. That test guards agent packages against coupling to framework internals; `execx` is a leaf with zero repo-internal deps (`go list -deps` confirms), and the test's own error message says to add intentional cases. Flagging it since it widens an architectural boundary — easy to revert if you'd rather the agent packages not reach for it.
- `mise run test:ci` has one failure, `TestCodexAppServerHooksList_BareWorktreeUsesLayoutRoot`. I confirmed it fails identically on clean `main` (stashed my work to check) — the known macOS `/var` vs `/private/var` issue, not from this change.
